_comment: RV-P1.4 T7 — hartland_cz declared-layer conformance corpus. Served from aliases.lex.yaml + skills/trend.md, compiled and packed by the REAL RV-P1.2 toolchain (LexiconValidator -> LexiconCompiler -> LexiconPacker) and read back through LexiconArchiveSource, so a red case here means the serving chain broke rather than that a fixture drifted. Queries run through the T5 Lookup surface. Classes: declared (a term reaches its target carrying the source, class and authored method it was written with), operator (an op: trigger from skill FRONTMATTER — the body must never appear, RV-35), method (EXACT/TYPOS(n) admission, RV-32/T4), tokens-margin (an ambiguous term is returned but never auto-bindable), member (the non-lexicon path, unchanged). The RV-39 layer tuple is asserted per-run, not per-case. Provenance: hand-authored 2026-08-03 against the hartland BM-arc Czech world (Brno/Praha/Ostrava/Plzen/Hradec Kralove DCs, CZK) and hartland's real md/er refs.

_note: The model-snapshot refs this estate's lexicon compiles against. `op:` refs are deliberately absent: they resolve by prefix and never touch the index (RV-38/RV-42), so an operator does not dangle against a snapshot that will never contain it.

_why: one dropped diacritic is one edit, inside the authored TYPOS(1)
two dropped diacritics is two edits — outside the authored TYPOS(1). The cap is the author's n, not the engine's own tolerance, and the folded index would otherwise score this a perfect hit
EXACT compares on the AUTHORED form, so a diacritic-stripped query is not the authored word — a TYPOS decision this author declined (T4)
a different word one edit away; EXACT is exactly what keeps it from reaching md.onHandQty
`tržby celkem` and `vratky celkem` share the token, the RV-32 margin falls under the floor, so both are returned and neither may be bound unattended
the non-lexicon path: a data value still wins on its own name, carries no target ref, no class, no authored method and no uniqueness decision
